caption: Coded research workflows of earth-science papers published in 2022, round 1 (n = 374 of 525 eligible papers with a valid coding; first coding) and round 2 (n = 198 of 222 eligible papers with a valid coding; tag r2). Each paper's full text was coded once by a language model (Claude Opus 5.5, sent as asynchronous batch requests) onto graph v0.4.2 of the modes of inquiry with codebook 1.5.0. A valid coding passes a format check (fields, allowed values, step order, quotes of 25 words or fewer), which says nothing about accuracy. The second coding of 50 gold-set papers (run-to-run test) is not used. 5 of 379 round-1 coding files fail the format check of tools/check_coding.py (quote over 25 words) and are excluded, as are 4 of 202 round-2 files. All measures use the final-paper sequence. (a) Share of papers that use each node at least once, nodes in graph order; error bars are 95% percentile bootstrap intervals over papers (2000 resamples, seed 2026). K (Keep) is coded in all 374 round-1 papers, so its percentile interval has zero width; a Wilson 95% interval for 374 of 374 is 0.990 to 1. (b) Number of coded steps per paper, steps as coded with consecutive repeats of a node not merged; the vertical line marks the median (22, 22). Merging consecutive repeats of a node gives a median of 20, 20. (c) Entry state of the paper. (d) Claim status at the end of the paper; the text at right gives the number and share of papers whose outcome was coded as contradicted (9, 2%; 2, 1%). In (c) and (d), legend labels give the number of papers in each category (round 1; round 2) and percentages are written in segments of 7% or more. In (c), Other pools data without theory (10; 3) and external goal (6; 1). No paper was coded forecast skill or none; these categories are not shown. Paper identifiers and file paths are in the provenance fields of this file.
